summary: Pressure and talk on several fronts: blasts in Iran, a new candidate to lead Israel, Ukraine-Russia talks on Tuesday, new Ebola vaccines, and COP31 opens.

question.text: COP31's host argues that if more of the world's energy comes from electricity, fossil fuel use will fall by itself. What would have to be true for that to work, and how could you tell if it was not?

read.title: COP31 Briefing: What to expect from the Antalya climate summit?
read.summary: A clear guide to the fights at this year's UN climate summit, from finance and adaptation to the fossil fuel roadmap, and who stands where.

topics.heading: Blasts hit Iran's Qeshm and Jask as Iran drops its missile-range limit
topics.summary: Iranian state media reported unexplained explosions on Qeshm Island and in the port of Jask on Saturday, a day after US strikes on Qeshm.[^1] Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they have lifted a self-imposed 2,000 km limit on missile range, while the US opened a new task force to squeeze Iran's supply routes.[^2][^3]

lead.title: Explosions heard in Strait of Hormuz as Iran reviews de-escalation proposals

alsoReported.title: IRGC claims a self-imposed limit on ballistic missile range 'has been lifted'
US releases video of strike on cargo ship in Gulf of Oman amid Iran blockade enforcement

article: On Saturday evening, Iranian state media reported two explosions on Qeshm, an island in the Strait of Hormuz, and several more in Jask, a port on the Gulf of Oman. The cause was unclear, and Iranian officials did not say the US was behind them.[^1] They came a day after President Trump confirmed what he called "minor" US strikes on an air-defence system on Qeshm.[^1][^2] On Sunday, Iran's military said two tankers caught fire after hitting mines on what it called an "unauthorised route"; this has not been independently confirmed.[^1]

Also on Saturday, a spokesman for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Iran's most powerful military force, said Iran's self-imposed 2,000 km limit on ballistic missile range "has been lifted". He did not say whether Iran has longer-range missiles.[^2] A 2,000 km range already reaches the whole Arabian Peninsula and parts of southeastern Europe.[^2]

The US is tightening its blockade of Iranian ports. Central Command (CENTCOM), the US military command for the Middle East, said an aircraft fired on the stern of a St Kitts-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman after it ignored warnings when leaving an Iranian port; it says the crew were told to move away first.[^3][^1] It also set up "Task Force Iron Gate" to target Iran's land routes and Caspian Sea trade in weapons and dual-use technology. CENTCOM says the blockade has stopped more than $25 billion in oil exports, a figure not independently checked.[^3]

Diplomacy continues alongside the pressure. Iran is reviewing Qatar's proposals, AP reports, and a former Pakistani ambassador says Iran has offered to limit uranium enrichment to 3.6%, a level used for power plants; that offer is reported by one outlet only.[^1][^4] A senior Iranian official insists talks cannot start until Iran's conditions, including lifted sanctions and released frozen assets, are met.[^4] My read: both sides are raising pressure to strengthen their hand before any talks, and the risk is that a mistake at sea turns pressure into wider fighting.
topics.differences: Iran says tankers hit mines on routes it had warned against and gives no cause for Saturday's blasts; the US has not commented on them.[^1] NBC, as reported by The Times of Israel, says some Trump advisers want major strikes to resume before January; the White House has not confirmed this.[^2]

topics.heading: Israel's president picks Gadi Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form the next government
topics.summary: President Isaac Herzog chose former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, backed by 67 of 120 lawmakers, to try to form Israel's next government; Benjamin Netanyahu had 46.[^5][^6] Eisenkot has 28 days, plus a possible 14, to find a majority.[^5]

lead.title: Israel's president picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form next government

alsoReported.title: Herzog taps Eisenkot to form next government
President Herzog taps Eisenkot to form coalition, but path remains fraught

article: On Saturday evening, Herzog told Gadi Eisenkot, a former army chief who now heads the Yashar party, that he would be asked to form a government. He is due to receive the mandate formally at a ceremony in Jerusalem on Sunday evening, Israel time.[^5][^7] In Israel's system, voters choose parties, and the president then asks the lawmaker most likely to build a majority of 61 in the 120-seat Knesset to try.[^5]

Sixty-seven lawmakers recommended Eisenkot, including members of Arab-led parties, against 46 for Netanyahu. The ultra-Orthodox party United Torah Judaism recommended no one.[^6] Recommending someone is not the same as joining his government. In the Oct 27 election, Eisenkot's alliance won 48 seats, Netanyahu's bloc 53, and Arab-led parties a record 19.[^5]

The path to 61 is hard. Eisenkot has ruled out governing with the Arab-led parties, so one route is to add the two ultra-Orthodox parties, which would give him exactly 61; one of them, Shas, calls reports that it might join "total fake news".[^5][^7] Another is a minority government supported from outside by Arab parties; Haaretz reports that Ra'am will back him, according to India's ANI news agency.[^5][^8] Eisenkot calls for a "national emergency government", while Netanyahu warns against a government that would depend on parties he calls supporters of terrorism.[^6][^7]

If Eisenkot fails, the president can give another lawmaker a turn, and if that fails too a new election would follow within 90 days, with Netanyahu staying on as caretaker.[^5] The new Knesset is sworn in on Tuesday.[^8] My read: whoever governs will shape the next phase in Gaza, but a coalition could take weeks, so little is likely to change there before December.
topics.differences: Netanyahu says a government relying on Arab parties would endanger the state; Arab party leader Ahmad Tibi expects a minority government they back from outside, and Eisenkot's party calls Netanyahu's appeal for unity "cynical".[^5][^6] Reports differ on the deadline: Israel Hayom gives Dec 6, or Dec 20 if extended.[^6]

topics.heading: Ukraine names Umerov to lead Abu Dhabi talks as both sides keep striking energy
topics.summary: Rustem Umerov will lead Ukraine's team at US-mediated talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11, the first since February.[^9][^10] Before them, Russia hit Ukraine's power grid again and Ukraine struck a Russian arms factory and refinery.[^10][^11]

lead.title: Zelenskyy Says Russia Seeks Blackout In Ukraine Ahead Of US-Mediated Talks In Abu Dhabi

alsoReported.title: Umerov to lead Ukraine delegation in Abu Dhabi peace talks despite media confusion, top official confirms
Zelenskyy accuses Russia of escalating strikes ahead of peace talks

article: Ukraine, Russia and the US are due to meet in Abu Dhabi, capital of the United Arab Emirates, on Nov 10 and 11, the first three-way talks since February.[^10][^11] A senior Ukrainian lawmaker, David Arakhamia, confirmed that Rustem Umerov, Ukraine's top negotiator, will lead its team, after some reports said intelligence chief turned chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov would. Budanov will attend and told CBS not to expect a big breakthrough.[^9] Russia's team includes Vladimir Medinsky, a Kremlin aide.[^10]

The talks follow one of the heaviest attacks this autumn. On Nov 7, Russia fired 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, and Al Jazeera reports that only four of the missiles were intercepted.[^11] President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia wants to "plunge the entire country into a blackout" by hitting substations that link nuclear plants to the grid.[^10] Russia's defence ministry says it targeted military, energy and transport sites.[^11] Ukraine, for its part, says its missiles hit a factory in Oryol, Russia, that makes parts for Iskander missiles, and a drone attack caused a fire at a refinery in Saratov.[^10]

The two sides remain far apart. Russia says fighting will stop only with a full peace deal that meets its territorial demands, including Ukraine giving up the whole Donbas region, and rejects an unconditional ceasefire.[^9][^10] President Trump says a "big, beautiful agreement" could be close, and US envoy Jared Kushner says any deal would respect Ukraine's sovereignty.[^10] European governments are not expected at the table, and EU leaders will discuss their role on Nov 13.[^9]

My read: these talks are a test of whether working-level contact can produce smaller steps, such as an energy truce or prisoner exchanges, rather than a full settlement. Watch whether attacks on power plants slow after the meeting, since that would matter most to Ukrainians this winter.
topics.differences: Ukraine says Russia is escalating attacks to gain leverage before the talks; Russia says it hits military-linked targets and that a Dnipro bridge it struck moved Ukrainian equipment.[^10][^11] Russia's claim to have downed 411 Ukrainian drones in one night has not been independently checked.[^10]

topics.heading: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 10,600 cases as strain-specific vaccines join a trial
topics.summary: The WHO says Congo has recorded 10,668 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,198 deaths, the largest outbreak in its history.[^12][^13] For the first time, two vaccines designed for this strain, Bundibugyo, will be tested during an outbreak of it.[^13]

lead.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya and Nigeria

alsoReported.title: Two new Ebola vaccines to join DR Congo clinical trial
WHO approves trials for two new Ebola vaccines

article: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which began in May, is the largest in the country's history.[^13] By Nov 3, the World Health Organization counted 10,668 confirmed cases and 5,198 deaths, nearly half of those infected, across eight provinces, with 1,463 new cases in the past three weeks.[^12] Most cases are in Ituri province in the northeast. Kenya has had nine cases and Nigeria one imported case.[^12]

This outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a less common type of Ebola. The only licensed Ebola vaccine, Ervebo, was made for a different type, Zaire, so it is uncertain how well it protects here.[^13] On Nov 4 and 5, the WHO said expert advisers had recommended adding two vaccines designed for Bundibugyo to a trial already under way: one from Oxford University and the Serum Institute of India, and one from Moderna using mRNA, the method behind some COVID-19 vaccines.[^13][^14]

The trial, called Tumaini ("hope" in Swahili), uses ring vaccination: health workers vaccinate the contacts of each confirmed case, and their contacts, to build a ring of protection around it.[^13] It began on Oct 23 in Bunia, the main city of Ituri. The new vaccines still need national approval, and results are expected in early 2027, according to South Africa's The National.[^13][^15] WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said vaccines "alone will not end this outbreak, but they could become a powerful new tool."[^13]

The WHO rates the risk as very high in Congo, high for its neighbours and low globally, and advises against travel bans, which it says punish countries for reporting outbreaks.[^12][^14] Fear of treatment centres and misinformation still keep some sick people away from care.[^15] My read: the vaccines are good news for the long term, but the next few months depend on the slower work of tracing contacts and building trust.

topics.heading: COP31 opens in Antalya with finance and an electrification goal at the centre
topics.summary: The UN climate summit runs from Nov 9 to 20 in Antalya, Turkey, the first since warming past 1.5C became almost certain.[^17][^18] Its host wants 35% of the world's energy to come from electricity by 2035, while poorer countries focus on promised money.[^17][^16]

lead.title: Ireland to take on central role at COP31 climate summit in Turkey

alsoReported.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?

article: Nearly 200 countries meet in Antalya from Monday for COP31, the yearly UN climate summit. Turkey hosts it and leads a programme of voluntary pledges, while Australia chairs the formal negotiations.[^17] It is the first COP held when exceeding the Paris Agreement goal of 1.5C of warming, at least for a time, is almost certain; Deutsche Welle reports that even full delivery of current national pledges points to up to 2.6C.[^17][^18]

The host's main idea is a goal for electricity to supply 35% of the world's final energy use by 2035, up from about 23 to 24% today, to be launched on Nov 10.[^17] Electric cars, heat pumps and industry running on electricity use energy more efficiently than burning fuel. Critics note the goal does not require that electricity be clean, and current policies point to about 28%.[^17] Brazil, last year's host, has also published a voluntary roadmap away from fossil fuels, which some countries want named in the final text and oil producers oppose.[^17]

Money may matter more than targets. Rich countries agreed in 2024 to provide $300 billion a year for poorer countries by 2035, and last year promised to triple funds for adapting to climate impacts, but there is no agreed starting figure for that tripling.[^16][^17] Ireland, which coordinates the EU's negotiators this time, says the EU wants to deliver on existing promises rather than set new ones; aid groups ask whether help will come as grants or as loans that add to debt.[^16]

China and India are not sending their top leaders.[^17] Some experts argue that progress now comes more from smaller groups of willing countries than from consensus at COPs.[^18] My read: success here will be measured less by headlines than by whether the finance and adaptation promises gain clear numbers.
topics.differences: Outlets give different figures for electricity's current share of energy use, from about 20% (DW, RTÉ) to 23-24% (Climate Home), likely because they measure it differently.[^16][^17][^18] The host says electrification will cut fossil fuel use on its own; campaigners say a separate fossil fuel commitment is needed.[^17]
